extracted.intended_audience: Internal CIA administrative staff (Chief, NF Administrative Staff; Chief, Publications & Presentations Group, NFAC) and agency policy implementers
extracted.subtask_description: An internal memorandum commenting on an OMB circular about instituting employee parking fees, arguing operational and equity considerations for exempting or reducing fees for certain shift workers in the Publications & Presentations Group (PPG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess burden of parking fees on PPG employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Parking fees, if instituted, will place a heavy burden on many PPG employees. PPG operates six days a week, twenty-four hours a day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate proposed parking fees with attention to groups whose work schedules (e.g., 24/7 operations) make fees particularly burdensome; quantify or qualitatively note the operating schedule and its effect on ability to avoid fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for lack of alternative transportation for second/third shift employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees who work the second and third shifts literally have no means to get to the Agency except by car.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When forming parking policy, consider whether public transit or other options exist for nonstandard shifts; if alternatives are absent, policies should not assume employees can switch to other transport modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider geographic dispersion and impracticality of car pools for night/irregular hours staff
rubrics_metrics.description: PPG night personnel or those who work irregular hours live in widely scattered areas in the metropolitan area. Car pools are all but impossible to form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete examples (e.g., Registry staff starting at 0500 or 0400) to demonstrate why car-pooling/public-transit assumptions fail; policy should incorporate the realities of employees' residential dispersion and shift start times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize job requirements that preclude participation in car pools
rubrics_metrics.description: In many instances job requirements are such that an individual cannot be in a car pool and must drive alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify roles whose duties (timing, security, obligations such as delivery of materials) make shared transport infeasible; avoid one-size-fits-all penalties for those roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not penalize employees required to perform duties after normal duty hours
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not feel that a person should be penalized by having to pay full parking costs because he or she is carrying out a job assignment, especially after normal duty hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy formulation should include an equity test for after-hours assignments; consider exemptions or mitigations for employees whose job assignments force them to seek solo car travel during off-hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage car pools and public transportation while providing exemptions where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: I agree that we should encourage car pools and the use of public transportation. I believe, however, that employees who work at night or have irregular hours should be exempted from parking fees or pay, at most, only nominal fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance incentive measures (promote car pools/public transit) with targeted relief (exemptions or nominal fees) for night/irregular-hour workers; specify criteria for who qualifies for exemptions (e.g., shift times, inability to carpool, essential solo transport duties).
